## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle *Sahasrabhuja* dhāraṇī-sūtra translated by **Bodhiruci** ([菩提流志](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E5%BF%97), d. 727), the South-Indian master who succeeded **Divākara** ([地婆訶羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%B0%E5%A9%86%E8%A8%B6%E7%BE%85)) as principal Sanskrit-translation lead in the [武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9)–[中宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%AD%E5%AE%97) courts (693–713). The text is parallel to and partly textually overlapping with [KR6j0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0256) (Zhìtōng's *Sahasrabhuja* sūtra) but is independently translated from Sanskrit and arranged around the *mātṛ-dhāraṇī-kāya* (姥陀羅尼身) — the "mother-dhāraṇī body" — i.e. the body of the bodhisattva understood as the locus of all dhāraṇīs.

**Abstract**

In the opening Avalokiteśvara, gazing toward the Buddha with respect, declares his "former-life inconceivable merit-cause" by which he received this dhāraṇī. The Buddha then expounds the *mātṛ-dhāraṇī* — the basic spell-formula — and the cultivator's procedure: visualisation of the bodhisattva, recitation, and the worldly fruits (cure of disease, exorcism, longevity, *abhaya*) and the supramundane fruits (good rebirth, eventual *bodhi*). The text is briefer and more focused than Zhìtōng's parallel ([KR6j0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0256)), confining itself to a single principal mantra and a small number of derivative formulae. Its Sanskrit original is best identified as a member of the **Nīlakaṇṭhaka-dhāraṇī** family, contemporaneous with the *Avalokiteśvaraikādaśa-mukha-dhāraṇī* and the *Cundī-dhāraṇī* that Bodhiruci was also rendering in the same translation series.

CANWWW (T20N1058) cross-references [KR6j0256](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0256)/[KR6j0257](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0257) (T20N1057, Zhìtōng) and [KR6j0269](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0269) (T20N1064) as related texts of the same *Sahasrabhuja* corpus.
